product.amstrad-pc6486sx.summary: Amstrad’s move to the 486SX for home users, sold with a software bundle for working in Windows.
product.amstrad-pc6486sx.history: The PC6486SX appears in the 1992 press as the 486SX renewal of Amstrad’s consumer offering. In June, Tilt presented it as part of a future 6000 range intended to replace the 5000. In September, Science & Vie Micro reported a French price of 13,990 francs including tax, MS-DOS 5, Windows 3 and Works. The magazine attributed manufacture to Southeast Asia without naming the contractor. In January 1993, British dealers were still advertising it with a 105 MB hard disk.
product.amstrad-pc6486sx.warning: Historical card under research; the preserved BIOS has no validated BluMach boot yet.
product.amstrad-pc6486sx.technical.marke: Reports and advertisements establish particular offers, not a launch day. Tilt documents the model in June 1992; SVM gives the French price in September and PCW a British offer in January 1993.
product.amstrad-pc6486sx.technical.confi: The offered configuration varies by source. Computers by Post advertises a 20 MHz 486SX, 4 MB and 105 MB in PCW; owner dekuNukem describes a specimen with a 25 MHz 486SX and 4 MB.
product.amstrad-pc6486sx.technical.cpu: Clock speeds differ across sources. Tilt states 16 MHz; SVM and the PCW advertisement, 20 MHz; the owner and his BIOS identifier, 25 MHz. These differences are not treated as proven factory revisions.
product.amstrad-pc6486sx.technical.board: The preserved board provides identification clues. The owner calls it CAM33-P2; his photograph shows a Chips & Technologies P82C206 and AMI labels. The BIOS contains CPM25P0,4,5; the complete board revision still needs verification.
product.amstrad-pc6486sx.technical.video: Video and connections depend on cards still needing identification. The owner describes a Trident ISA card and an I/O card; the controller model and an attributable video ROM for that specimen are missing.
product.amstrad-pc6486sx.technical.firmw: A 64 KiB system BIOS is preserved. The owner reports physically reading a 27C512 with a TL866II Plus; its SHA-256 matches the preserved file. Rights remain unresolved.
product.amstrad-pc6486sx.technical.ident: The file identifies itself as Amstrad, which does not certify operation. Offset 0x150 contains “AMSTRAD plc PC6486SX25, 07/10/1992” and 0xF0 contains “CPM25P0,4,5”. These are file offsets; the date is retained literally without inferring a launch date.
product.amstrad-pc6486sx.technical.verif: Documents, photograph and bytes were checked without executing firmware. BluMach 88f74ba3 has no dedicated pc6486sx registration; matching hashes establish integrity, not booting.
product.amstrad-pc6486sx.technical.limit: A board map, identified video controller and boot validation are missing. The BIOS remains unscanned for malware; no image has clear publication rights and no complete configuration is validated.
product.amstrad-pc6486sx.technical.press: Tilt no. 103, June 1992, p. 42, “Amstrad : Quel avenir ?”: consumer positioning, 6000 range and 16 MHz.
product.amstrad-pc6486sx.technical.svm: Martine Guenzet, SVM no. 97, September 1992, pp. 48–49, “Amstrad joue la carte Intel”: French offer, 20 MHz, software and manufacturing region.
product.amstrad-pc6486sx.technical.adver: Computers by Post advertisement, Personal Computer World, January 1993, PDF p. 119: 20 MHz, 4 MB and 105 MB disk.
product.amstrad-pc6486sx.technical.owner: dekuNukem, Vintage Computer ROM Dumps, revision ca6c8117: specimen description, photograph and BIOS; added to the archive on 22 November 2022, not a launch date.
product.amstrad-pc6486sx.technical.sourc: BluMach 88f74ba3, machine_table.c and m_amstrad.c: machine-registration inspection, without a boot test.
